title: Pljeskavica with roast potatoes and ajvar
description: Big, juicy Balkan meat patties seasoned with onion and garlic, served with roast potatoes, ajvar and raw onion.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220 °C. Cut the potatoes into wedges, toss them on a tray with {2 tbsp} of the oil and half the salt, and roast for 35 minutes, turning once.
steps.tip: Spread them out so they crisp instead of steaming.

steps.text: Grate one onion very finely and squeeze out the juice. Crush the garlic. Mix them into the meat with the rest of the salt, the pepper and a pinch of baking soda, and knead for 2 minutes.
steps.tip: Kneading makes the meat springy, and the pinch of baking soda keeps pljeskavica juicy. Both are old grill-house tricks.

steps: Divide into 4 balls and press each one into a thin, wide patty, about 1 cm thick.

steps.text: Heat the rest of the oil in a large frying pan or grill pan on medium-high. Fry the patties for 4 to 5 minutes on each side until browned and cooked through.
steps.tip: Press a dip into the middle with your thumb before frying so they stay flat.

steps: Slice the second onion thinly. Serve the pljeskavica with the potatoes, a spoon of ajvar and raw onion.

title: Ražnjići with rice and ajvar
description: Pork skewers with onion and pepper, marinated in paprika and oil, pan-grilled and served with rice and ajvar.

steps.text: Cut the pork into 3 cm cubes and mix with {2 tbsp} of the oil, the paprika, crushed garlic and salt. Leave for 15 minutes.
steps.tip: Pork neck stays juicy on skewers. Leaner cuts dry out.

steps.text: Meanwhile cook the rice: rinse it, put it in a pot with {450 ml} water and a pinch of salt, bring to the boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat.
steps.tip: Keeping the lid on is what makes rice fluffy.

steps.text: Cut the onion and pepper into squares and thread them onto skewers, alternating with the meat.
steps.tip: Wooden skewers? Soak them in water for 10 minutes first so they do not burn. No skewers? Fry the pieces loose.

steps.text: Heat a grill pan or large frying pan on medium-high with the rest of the oil. Cook the skewers for 10 to 12 minutes, turning every few minutes, until browned and cooked through.
steps.tip: Cut a cube in half to check: no pink inside.

steps: Serve with the rice and ajvar.

title: Turkey steaks in mushroom sauce with mash
description: Tender turkey steaks in a creamy mushroom sauce, with buttery mashed potatoes. A classic Croatian restaurant lunch at home.
steps: Peel the potatoes, cut them into chunks and boil them in salted water for 20 minutes until soft.

steps.text: Slice the turkey into steaks about 1 cm thick, season with half the salt and the pepper, and dust lightly with the flour.
steps.tip: The flour gives a golden crust and later thickens the sauce.

steps.text: Heat the oil and half the butter in a large frying pan on medium-high. Fry the turkey for 3 minutes on each side until golden, then lift it out.
steps.tip: Turkey dries out quickly, so it only needs to be just cooked.

steps: In the same pan, fry the chopped onion and sliced mushrooms for 8 minutes until golden. Pour in the cream and {100 ml} water, add the rest of the salt and simmer for 3 minutes.
Put the turkey back in the sauce for 2 minutes to warm through. Scatter with parsley.
Drain the potatoes and mash them with the warm milk and the rest of the butter. Serve with the turkey and plenty of sauce.

title: Pohani oslić with potato salad
description: Hake fillets in a crisp breadcrumb coat with a Dalmatian potato salad of onion, olive oil and vinegar. A Friday classic.

ingredients.note: for frying, some stays in the pan

steps: Boil the potatoes in their skins in salted water for 20 minutes until a knife slides in. Peel them while warm and slice into a bowl.

steps.text: Add the thinly sliced onion, olive oil, vinegar, parsley and half the salt to the warm potatoes and mix gently.
steps.tip: Warm potatoes soak up the dressing much better than cold ones.

steps.text: Pat the hake dry and season with the rest of the salt. Coat each piece in flour, then beaten egg, then breadcrumbs.
steps.tip: Thaw frozen hake in the fridge overnight and dry it very well, or the coating slides off.

steps.text: Heat the sunflower oil in a large frying pan on medium-high. Fry the fish for 3 to 4 minutes on each side until golden. Drain on kitchen paper.
steps.tip: The oil is ready when a breadcrumb sizzles at once. Never leave hot oil alone.

steps: Serve with the potato salad and lemon wedges.

title: Roast pork neck with potatoes and cabbage salad
description: A Sunday roast the Croatian way: pork neck slowly roasted with garlic and rosemary on potatoes, with a sharp cabbage salad.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180 °C. Rub the pork with {1 tbsp} of the oil, the paprika, rosemary, pepper and most of the salt. Make small cuts and push in slices of garlic.
steps.tip: Season it the evening before if you can: the salt seasons the meat all the way through.

steps: Put the pork in a roasting tin with {200 ml} water, cover with foil and roast for 1 hour.
Cut the potatoes and onions into chunks, toss them with the rest of the oil and a pinch of salt and add them around the meat.

steps.text: Uncover, turn the oven up to 200 °C and roast for 45 minutes more, turning the potatoes once, until the meat is browned and tender.
steps.tip: It is done when a fork slides into the meat easily. Add a splash of water if the tin dries out.

steps: Meanwhile shred the cabbage very thinly, mix it with the vinegar, a pinch of salt and a little oil and squeeze it with your hands for a moment.

steps.text: Rest the meat for 10 minutes, then slice it and serve with the potatoes, the juices from the tin and the cabbage salad.
steps.tip: Leftover slices make great sandwiches. It keeps 3 days.

title: Honey mustard chicken traybake
description: Chicken legs roasted on potatoes and carrots in a sticky honey and mustard glaze. One tray, almost no washing up.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Cut the potatoes into chunks, the carrots into thick slices and the onions into wedges.
Toss the vegetables on a large tray with the olive oil, thyme and half the salt.

steps.text: Mix the honey, mustard, crushed garlic and the rest of the salt. Rub half of it over the chicken legs and lay them on the vegetables, skin side up.
steps.tip: Keep the other half of the glaze for later: honey burns if it goes in at the start.

steps: Roast for 35 minutes.

steps.text: Brush the chicken with the rest of the glaze, turn the vegetables, and roast for 15 minutes more until sticky and golden.
steps.tip: The chicken is done when the juices run clear near the bone.

steps: Serve straight from the tray, with the pan juices spooned over.

title: Greek moussaka
description: Layers of fried eggplant and cinnamon-spiced beef sauce under a thick, golden béchamel. A weekend project that feeds you for days.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Slice the eggplants 1 cm thick, lay them on two oiled trays, brush with most of the olive oil, sprinkle with a little salt and roast for 25 minutes until soft and golden.
steps.tip: Roasting instead of frying uses much less oil and is easier.

steps: Meanwhile fry the chopped onion in the rest of the oil for 6 minutes, add the beef and brown it for 8 minutes, breaking it up. Add the garlic, cinnamon and oregano for a few seconds.

steps.text: Add the tomatoes and half the remaining salt and simmer for 20 minutes until thick.
steps.tip: The sauce should be thick, not watery, or the moussaka will not hold its layers.

steps.text: Make the béchamel: melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk a little at a time. Simmer for 5 minutes until thick. Off the heat, whisk in the egg, half the parmesan, the nutmeg and the rest of the salt.
steps.tip: Let it cool for a minute before adding the egg, so it does not scramble.

steps: Turn the oven down to 180 °C. Layer half the eggplant, all the meat sauce and the rest of the eggplant in a baking dish. Pour the béchamel over and sprinkle with the rest of the parmesan.

steps.text: Bake for 40 minutes until deep golden. Let it rest for at least 20 minutes before cutting.
steps.tip: Resting lets it set into neat slices. It is even better the next day and keeps 3 days.

title: Goveđa juha (beef soup with noodles)
description: The Sunday beef soup: a clear, golden broth simmered for hours with root vegetables, served with fine noodles, and the beef with horseradish.

steps.text: Put the beef in a big pot with {3000 ml} cold water and bring it slowly to a simmer. Skim off the grey foam as it rises.
steps.tip: Starting in cold water and heating slowly gives a clear, tasty broth.

steps.text: Halve the onion and brown the cut sides in a dry pan until almost black, then add it to the pot with the peeled whole carrots, parsnip, celeriac, bay leaves, salt and pepper.
steps.tip: The charred onion gives the soup its golden colour.

steps.text: Simmer very gently, lid half on, for 2.5 hours.
steps.tip: Only a few small bubbles should rise. Boiling hard makes the soup cloudy.

steps: Lift out the meat and vegetables and pour the broth through a sieve into another pot.
Bring the broth to the boil, add the noodles and cook until soft, 3 to 5 minutes. Slice the carrots back in and add the chopped parsley.

steps.text: Serve the soup first, then the beef sliced, with horseradish and the vegetables.
steps.tip: That is how Croatian Sunday lunch starts. The broth keeps 4 days; cook fresh noodles each time.

title: Riblja juha (Dalmatian fish soup)
description: A light Dalmatian fish soup with potato, carrot, a little rice, white wine and lots of parsley and lemon.
steps: Chop the onion and garlic, dice the potatoes and carrot and chop the parsley. Cut the fish into large chunks.
Heat the olive oil in a pot on medium and soften the onion and carrot for 6 minutes. Add the garlic and tomato paste for a few seconds.
Pour in the wine and let it bubble for 1 minute. Add the potatoes, rice, bay leaves, salt and {1300 ml} water and simmer for 15 minutes.

steps.text: Add the fish and simmer gently for 8 minutes, until it flakes.
steps.tip: Do not stir hard, so the fish stays in nice pieces.

steps.text: Stir in the parsley, squeeze in the lemon and serve with bread.
steps.tip: A few drops of good olive oil on each bowl is the Dalmatian finish.

title: Burek s mesom (meat filo pie)
description: Thin filo rolled around seasoned minced meat and onion, baked until crisp and golden. Eaten with plain yogurt, any time of day.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C and oil a round baking tin or tray. Chop the onions very finely.

steps.text: Mix the raw meat with the onions, salt, pepper and {4 tbsp} water with your hand.
steps.tip: In burek the meat goes in raw. The water keeps the filling juicy as it bakes.

steps.text: Lay 2 sheets of filo on top of each other and brush them lightly with oil. Put a line of filling along one long edge and roll up loosely into a long sausage.
steps.tip: Keep the filo you are not using under a damp towel: it dries out and cracks quickly.

steps: Coil the roll into a snail shape in the middle of the tin, or lay rolls side by side. Repeat with the rest of the filo and filling.

steps.text: Brush the top with the rest of the oil and bake for 40 to 45 minutes until deep golden and crisp.
steps.tip: Sprinkle a little water over it for the last 5 minutes and cover with a towel after baking: the inner layers soften like a real bakery burek.

steps: Let it rest for 10 minutes, cut into pieces and serve with plain yogurt.

title: Ham and leek quiche
description: Crisp homemade pastry filled with soft leeks, ham, cheese and a creamy egg custard. Good warm or cold.

steps.text: Rub {100 g} of the cold butter into the flour with half the salt until it looks like breadcrumbs. Add about {3 tbsp} cold water and press into a dough. Wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
steps.tip: Cold butter and only a little water make crisp pastry. Do not knead it.

steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C. Roll the pastry out and line a 24 cm tart tin. Prick the base with a fork, line with baking paper and dried beans or rice and bake for 15 minutes. Remove the paper and beans and bake for 5 minutes more.

steps.text: Meanwhile slice the leek, wash it well and soften it in the rest of the butter for 8 minutes. Dice the ham and grate the cheese.
steps.tip: Pre-baking the empty case keeps the bottom crisp, not soggy.

steps: Whisk the eggs with the cream, milk, nutmeg and the rest of the salt.
Scatter the leek, ham and cheese in the pastry case and pour the egg mix over.

steps.text: Bake for 30 minutes until just set with a slight wobble in the middle. Cool for 10 minutes and serve with a green salad.
steps.tip: It keeps 2 days and makes a good packed lunch.

title: Homemade pizza with ham and mushrooms
description: A simple yeast dough, a thin tomato sauce, mozzarella, ham and mushrooms, baked on trays at home. Better and cheaper than delivery.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and {1 tsp} of the salt. Add {320 ml} lukewarm water and {2 tbsp} of the oil and knead for 8 minutes into a smooth, soft dough.
steps.tip: The dough should be slightly sticky. Lukewarm water, not hot: hot water kills the yeast.

steps: Cover the bowl and leave it somewhere warm for 1 hour, until doubled in size.

steps.text: Heat the oven to its highest setting (250 °C if possible) with the trays inside. Mix the passata with the oregano, the rest of the salt and oil.
steps.tip: A very hot oven and hot tray give a crisp base.

steps: Divide the dough in two and stretch each half thinly on baking paper with your fingers.

steps.text: Spread with a thin layer of sauce, then torn mozzarella, ham and sliced mushrooms.
steps.tip: Go easy on the sauce: too much makes a soggy pizza.

steps.text: Slide each pizza on its paper onto a hot tray and bake for 10 to 12 minutes until the edges are golden and the cheese bubbles.
steps.tip: Add rocket or a drizzle of olive oil after baking if you like.

title: Greek salad with chickpeas and pita
description: Tomato, cucumber, pepper, olives and a slab of feta with chickpeas for protein, oregano and olive oil, with warm flatbread.

ingredients.note: red onion if you have it

steps: Cut the tomatoes into wedges, the cucumber into thick half moons and the pepper into rings. Slice the onion thinly. Drain and rinse the chickpeas.

steps.text: Mix the vegetables, chickpeas and olives in a bowl with a pinch of salt, the vinegar and most of the olive oil.
steps.tip: Salt the tomatoes a few minutes before serving: their juice mixes with the oil into a dressing worth dipping bread into.

steps: Put the feta on top in one piece, sprinkle with oregano and drizzle with the rest of the oil.
Warm the flatbreads in a dry pan for a few seconds each side and serve alongside.

title: Roasted vegetable and quinoa salad with feta
description: Roasted zucchini, pepper, eggplant and onion with quinoa, chickpeas, feta and a lemon dressing. Great for lunch boxes.
steps: Heat the oven to 210 °C. Cut the zucchini, peppers, eggplant and onion into 2 cm pieces.

steps.text: Toss the vegetables on a large tray with {2 tbsp} of the oil and half the salt and roast for 30 minutes, turning once, until soft and browned at the edges.
steps.tip: Use two trays if they are crowded, so they roast instead of steam.

steps.text: Meanwhile rinse the quinoa in a sieve and simmer it in {500 ml} water with a pinch of salt for 15 minutes, until the water is gone. Cover and leave for 5 minutes.
steps.tip: Rinsing removes the bitter coating on the seeds.

steps: Whisk the rest of the oil with the lemon juice and the rest of the salt.

steps.text: Mix the quinoa, roasted vegetables, drained chickpeas, parsley and dressing. Crumble the feta over the top.
steps.tip: It keeps 3 days in the fridge and tastes good cold.

title: Lentil salad with feta and roasted peppers
description: Brown lentils dressed while warm with mustard vinaigrette, with roasted peppers, tomato, red onion, parsley and feta.

ingredients.note: red onion if you have it

steps.text: Rinse the lentils and simmer them in plenty of water with the bay leaves for 20 to 25 minutes until just tender. Drain.
steps.tip: Do not salt the water: salt added early can keep lentils hard. They should keep their shape.

steps: Whisk the olive oil, vinegar, mustard and salt in a large bowl. Add the warm lentils and mix.

steps.text: Slice the roasted peppers, dice the tomatoes, slice the onion thinly and chop the parsley. Mix them in.
steps.tip: Warm lentils soak up the dressing, so dress them first.

steps.text: Crumble the feta over the top and serve with bread.
steps.tip: It keeps 3 days and is even better the next day.

title: Beef and broccoli with rice
description: Thin strips of beef and crunchy broccoli in a glossy garlic, ginger and soy sauce, over rice. Faster than a takeaway.

steps.text: Start the rice: rinse it, put it in a pot with {550 ml} water and a pinch of salt, bring to the boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat.
steps.tip: Keeping the lid on is what makes rice fluffy.

steps.text: Slice the beef very thinly across the grain and toss it with half the cornstarch and {1 tbsp} of the soy sauce.
steps.tip: Put the beef in the freezer for 20 minutes first: it slices much more thinly.

steps: Mix the rest of the soy sauce and cornstarch with the honey, grated garlic and ginger and {100 ml} water. Cut the broccoli into small florets.

steps.text: Heat half the oil in a wok or large frying pan on high until smoking. Fry the beef in two batches for 2 minutes each until browned. Lift it out.
steps.tip: Very hot pan, small batches: that is how it browns instead of stewing.

steps: Add the rest of the oil and the broccoli with a splash of water, cover and steam-fry for 3 minutes until bright green.
Pour in the sauce, add the beef and toss for 1 minute until glossy. Serve over the rice with sesame seeds and sliced spring onion.

title: Baked savoury palačinke with ham and cheese
description: Palačinke rolled around ham and cheese, covered with cream and baked until bubbling. A favourite Croatian lunch from leftovers.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, two of the eggs, the salt and a little of the milk into a smooth paste, then whisk in the rest of the milk and {1 tbsp} of the oil. Rest for 10 minutes.
steps.tip: Adding the milk slowly is the trick to a batter without lumps.

steps.text: Fry thin palačinke in a hot pan wiped with oil, about 1 minute on the first side and a few seconds on the second. Stack them.
steps.tip: The first one is often a bad one. It is the cook's treat.

steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Grate the cheese. Lay a slice of ham and some cheese on each palačinka, roll it up and lay them side by side in an oiled baking dish.
Whisk the cream with the last egg and pour it over. Scatter the rest of the cheese on top.

steps.text: Bake for 20 minutes until golden and bubbling. Serve with a green salad.
steps.tip: Leftover palačinke from yesterday are perfect for this.
